method: The listed 75g dry egg noodles is an uncooked weight. Cut the 90g broccoli into small florets. Bring a saucepan of water to the boil, cook the broccoli for 3–4 minutes until just tender, then lift it onto a plate with a slotted spoon. Cook the noodles in the same boiling water for the time on their packet until tender, then drain well. Time this to finish shortly before the pan ingredients are ready.
Deseed and thinly slice the 90g mixed peppers. Check the 150g salmon fillet for bones. Keep it as a fillet for pan cooking, then flake it after cooking.

Heat half the listed olive oil in a non-stick frying pan over a medium heat. Put in the salmon fillet, skin-side down if it has skin. Cook for 4–5 minutes, turn carefully and cook for another 3–5 minutes until the centre is opaque, steaming hot and flakes easily; a thicker piece needs longer. Transfer to a clean plate; keep the pan for the vegetables. Never reuse the plate or utensils that held the raw food without washing them.

Add the remaining half of the listed olive oil to the same pan. Add 90g mixed peppers and cook for 4–6 minutes, stirring often, until softened with some bite. Keep the heat moderate so the small measured amount of oil does not smoke.
Add the drained noodles and broccoli to the pan. Toss gently for 1–2 minutes to combine without crushing the florets.

Turn the heat to low and fold in the 40g harissa tomato sauce. Stir for 1–2 minutes until hot, following any longer heating instruction on the sauce label. This measured sauce coats the food; do not boil it dry or add an unlisted jar of sauce.

Flake the cooked salmon into large pieces and fold into the pan at the end; avoid breaking it up with vigorous stirring. Heat gently until the whole pan is steaming hot, folding carefully so the seafood stays intact. Divide the noodles, vegetables and salmon fillet between serving bowls. Serve immediately.
